...craving world governs itself and boasts of great, high wisdom and gifts; it flaunts and parades these, imagining that the heavens would fall if it did not exist. Yet it is all nothing but a false, heathenish, and deadly philosophy <note>original: "Philoſophey"</note>. In the sight of God, this is a loathsome sin and a stinking, presumed wisdom that is pure folly before Him—as Paul says—and can never stand before the throne of God or dare to show itself. Likewise, there are many stinking, rotten, stagnant cisterns, puddles, and pools flowing from the dead sea <note>original: "toden Möhr," likely a reference to the Dead Sea or a stagnant marsh representing the realm of spiritual death.</note> and the dark kingdom of Satan, containing nothing but devilish poison and gall. Indeed, many thousands of people, in their ignorance and great blindness, drink temporal and eternal death from them, while still believing them to be healthy, wholesome wells and springs of water.

Because I have sought such a spring of truth and the living fountain of true wisdom and philosophy with great diligence and earnestness since my youth: I was also initially directed and drawn toward the rotten, foul, stinking puddles of the world-wise philosophy and arts. However, through divine gracious providence <note>original: "Providentz"</note> and the guidance of the Heavenly Father, I was fatherly rescued and turned away from such murky, dark cisterns. Finally, I reached the highly enlightened philosopher and monarch of the arts, **THEOPHRASTUS** <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and alchemist who revolutionized medicine and spiritual philosophy.</note>, who fundamentally explained and set before me the Light of Nature <term>Light of Nature: In Paracelsian thought, this is the divine wisdom "impressed" upon the natural world, which allows humans to understand the mysteries of creation through observation and spiritual insight.</term> in Astronomy, Philosophy, Magic, and Cabalistic Theology <note>original: "Astronomia, Philosophia, Magia, & Theologia Cabaliſtica"</note>. This foundation may never be contradicted in all eternity. And then I also reached Him who speaks in the New Testament (John, chapter 4) to the Samaritan woman, saying that He can give living water, and to whomever He gives it, it shall become in them a well of water springing up into eternal life; and whoever drinks of this water shall never thirst again. # Preface

Father from heaven called, <note>original: "Vatter vom Himmel gerüffen"</note> *Matthew 3: "Hear him, hear him, I say."* <note>original: "Hunc, Hunc, inquam, audite." This refers to the voice from heaven at Christ’s baptism: "This is my beloved Son, listen to him."</note> He who also says himself in *John 14*: "I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life; no one comes to the Father except through me," etc. Now, for many years, my dear hearts and brothers (as I have for several years now returned to the true, natural <term>Spagyric</term> <note>The "Spagyric" art refers to Paracelsian alchemy, which focuses on the separation and recombination of natural substances to create medicines.</note> philosophy), it has been my desire to taste with you from the cup of the prophets *Ezra* and *Joseph*, or even from the <term>Potable Gold of Moses</term> <note>original: "Auro potabili Mosis." This refers to the biblical account of Moses grinding the golden calf into powder and making the Israelites drink it (Exodus 32:20), which alchemists interpreted as a secret chemical process.</note>, which he strewed upon the water from the crushed golden calf and gave to the children of Israel to drink; also to drink the heavenly, fiery *Nectar* and the natural fountain of temporal life and health, which is granted to so few.

That this has not yet come to pass is truly our own fault: that we do not worthily and capably <term>prepare</term> <note>original: "præparieren"</note> and ready ourselves for it, and have instead, with the rest of the world, only chased and strived after temporal things until now, failing to heed the rule of CHRIST in *Matthew 6*: *"Seek first the kingdom of GOD and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you,"* etc. <note>original: "Quærite primùm regnum DEI & iustitiam eius, & cætera omnia adijcientur vobis, &c."</note> Indeed, we have even forgotten the first three <term>Cabalistic</term> <note>The author uses "Cabalistic" here to refer to the spiritual-mystical interpretation of scripture as it relates to natural secrets.</note> principles: *Ask, Seek, Knock.* <note>original: "Petite, Quærite, Pulsate."</note> Had we done this with diligence and led a Christian, godly, and God-pleasing life, while also better researching and fathoming Nature, we would without doubt have obtained something from the gold-rich fountain of grace within bountiful Nature.

However, as far as I can gather from all the *writings* of the philosophers who have written until now—among heathens and Christians—concerning the <term>Universal Medicine</term> <note>A legendary substance, often synonymous with the Philosopher's Stone, believed to cure all diseases.</note> and the blessed <term>Tincture</term> treasure, and who have possessed the **Philosopher’s Stone** as the highest secret treasure of Nature: I find that they were mostly all true Naturalists, deep-thinking *Philosophers*, *Magi*, and Cabalists. For true, right *Magic* <note>original: "Magia"</note> is such an art and skill through which one attains the knowledge of the elements, their composite bodies, fruits, properties, powers, and hidden effects.

# Preface

But the Cabala, from the high content of its high, secret understanding, shows the right path and road for man to reach God the Lord; how one should interact with Him, and what one should reveal and proclaim from His Word. **MAGIC** directs itself according to the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "Anima mundi"</note> and the natural spirit of the natural light: if one could lure this [spirit] forth from the **creatures** <note>original: "Creatis"</note> and creations of God, primarily from **metals** <note>original: "Metallis"</note> and **minerals** <note>original: "Mineralibus"</note>, and bring it to an **incombustible oil** <note>original: "Incombustibili oleo." In alchemy, this refers to a "perpetual" oil that represents the radical moisture or the quintessence, which cannot be destroyed by fire.</note>, then man would be helped. **CABALA**, however, directs itself according to the light of the **Holy Spirit**, which is ignited from above in the hearts of the believers: and faith must spring and flow forth from the **holy fountain** <note>original: "H. Fontina"</note> of the Word of God, and from the living water-source of **CHRIST (John 4)**, which will then lead us into eternal life, where we shall enjoy, drink, and eat with **CHRIST** in His kingdom the **new Divine Nectar**, and **heavenly Ambrosia, Manna**, and **bread of angels**.

Now, in order to partake eternally in such graces—from the natural **tincture-well** of health and all riches here in time, and then also from the **fountain** <note>original: "Fontin"</note> of heavenly grace, the living water and **divine nectar** <note>original: "Nectaris divini"</note> in the kingdom of **CHRIST**—we must apply ourselves to the matter differently: as far as nature is concerned, we must follow in the footsteps of **Theophrastus [Paracelsus], Roger Bacon, Friar Basilius [Valentinus], Isaac Hollandus**, etc., and other philosophers. As far as eternity is concerned, we must follow **CHRIST JESUS** as the **Thrice-Greatest** <note>original: "Trismegisto," a reference to Hermes Trismegistus, here identifying Christ as the ultimate source of all Hermetic and Spagyric wisdom.</note>, the **Spagyrist** <note>The author presents Christ as the supreme alchemist or "Spagyrist" who separates the soul from the dross of sin.</note>, the **Philosopher**, and the **Physician of body and soul**. We must study His command to **"Follow me"** <note>original: "Sequere me"</note>, and let these three also be our concern: **"ask, seek, knock"** <note>original: "petere, quærere, pulsare," referencing Matthew 7:7</note>; and we must keep His great New Commandment, which is but a light and easy burden: namely, to love God with all our heart, with all our soul, with all our mind, and with all our strength, and our neighbor as ourselves, etc.

**Likewise**, we must be found to be faithful and diligent students in the eight virtues of blessedness <note>The Beatitudes from the Sermon on the Mount.</note>, hearing **CHRIST** alone, and following no man, nor human wisdom and its spirit, for it is written: **"Cursed is he who trusts in man,"** <note>original: "Maledictus qui confidit in Homine," from Jeremiah 17:5.</note>

# Preface

...tion for this is laid before us by our highly enlightened Magus and Cabalist **THEOPHRASTUS** <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), the Swiss physician and alchemist who revolutionized medicine.</note>, from the Angelic and Cabalistic science <note>original: "Scientia"</note>, to whom all true Christian-minded philosophers should rightly give credence. Likewise, he who does not know Nature does not love her; he who thus recognizes nothing sees nothing in her, despises her, and his belly is his only God. The more knowledge there is in a thing, however, the more love for it is ignited. He who does not understand or recognize the poor, or has not experienced poverty himself, does not believe him, does not love him, and does nothing good for him—just as the pagan Queen Dido boasts in Virgil, saying: *Being no stranger to misfortune, I learn to help the wretched.* <note>original: "Non ignara mali miseris succurrere disco" (Latin). This quote from Virgil’s Aeneid emphasizes that personal suffering breeds empathy.</note>

This is much more appropriate for us Christians, by the command of our Master and Lord **JESUS CHRIST**; but, alas, God have mercy, such love and faithfulness have almost entirely grown cold and vanished in the hearts of all men. Therefore all things lie in knowledge; from this knowledge flow the fruits toward that thing. Knowledge gives Faith: for he who recognizes God believes in Him; he who does not recognize Him does not believe in Him. Therefore every person believes only as much as he knows.

Likewise in **alchemy**: he who does not learn to recognize it—its nature and its hidden, secret powers deep within metals and minerals—will not love it, much less be able to extract it, or know how to separate the *pure from the impure* <note>original: "Purum ab impuro"</note>, much less attain the **fifth essence** <term>fifth essence: Also known as the "quintessence," this is the purest, most concentrated medicinal force extracted from a substance, leaving the "impure" dross behind.</term>, which is the entire core and foundation in every being or created thing. And let this be enough philosophizing for now, until our joyful gathering and face-to-face conversation.

But since I am well and heartily disposed toward all *sons of the spagyric doctrine* <note>original: "Filiis doctrinæ Spagyricæ" (Latin). "Spagyric" is a term for alchemy involving the separation and recombination of natural elements.</note>, and am entirely inclined to promote, as much as possible with my help, their noble and honorable intent to obtain the precious treasure of the **Tincture** <note>The "Tincture" refers to the Philosopher's Stone in its liquid or transformative form, capable of healing or transmutation.</note> and the **Universal Medicine**, or even just to attain something in particular—I have once again decorated and planted a new Olympic Rose Garden <note>The "Rosarium" or Rose Garden is a common alchemical metaphor for a collection of wisdom or the stages of the Great Work.</note>, containing excellent little plants and little trees of both ancient and new

# Preface

...ze the writings the philosophers have left behind and established for us, which treat and discuss the blessed <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>The legendary substance sought by alchemists, said to be capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life or spiritual perfection.</note>, and the <term>Golden Branch of the Philosophers</term> <note>original: "Guldenen Ramo Philosophorum." A reference to the "Golden Bough" from Virgil’s Aeneid, used here as a metaphor for the rare and hidden knowledge required to enter the "garden" of alchemical secrets.</note>, explaining how the same may be plucked and obtained from the secret <term>Garden</term> <note>original: "Horto." Often used to describe the "Philosophical Garden" where the ingredients of the Great Work grow.</note> and from the <term>Tree of the Hesperides</term> <note>original: "Arbore Hesperidum." In Greek mythology, the Hesperides guarded a tree of golden apples; in alchemy, this represents the difficult and guarded path to the ultimate goal.</note>. I have divided this little book into two distinct parts: the first part I have set forth in public print under your honorable names, and to all of you, as my highly favorable, benevolent, dear Lords and friends, I dedicate it with well-meaning intent as a New Year's gift, <term>by right and title of dedication</term> <note>original: "dedicatorio titulo & jure."</note>. I have wished to publicly edit and declare this <term>as a public token of a grateful mind</term> <note>original: "quasi publicum gratæ mentis Symbolum."</note>, on account of all the manifold favors and good deeds, as well as the honor, love, and friendship shown to me. 

In the certain hope that Your High and Reverend, Honorable, Dear, and Gracious Excellencies will perceive this my well-meaning <term>Dedication</term> from me—a poor <term>student of Natural and immortal Philosophy</term> <note>original: "Philosophiæ Naturalis & immortalis alumno."</note> and <term>untiring disciple</term> <note>original: "Discipulo indefesso."</note>—in the best possible way. I ask that you might, as has happened abundantly until now, continue to recommend me and mine in all honor and through your manifold demonstrated friendship, toward all Christian love and faithful promotion in my <term>Eremitic</term> <note>Living the life of a hermit or a solitary spiritual seeker.</note> pilgrimage. Herewith, I <term>commend</term> <note>original: "commendierendt."</note> us all to the protection of Divine Grace. 

Done at Hagenau, 28 <term>December</term>, in the <term>year</term> 1607, in the <term>Old Julian Style</term> <note>original: "Stylo Veteri Iuliano." The Julian calendar was still used by many in the early 17th century before the full adoption of the Gregorian calendar.</note>, etc.

# TRACT 1.

## Containing the Practice of the Most Wise King Solomon, concerning the Philosopher's Stone.

If you wish for the **fixed** and the **unfixed** <note>original: "fire vnd vnfire." In alchemy, "fixed" (fir) refers to a substance that remains stable and does not evaporate when heated, while "unfixed" or "volatile" refers to substances that easily transform into vapor.</note> to become fixed together, <note>original: "ut facilem fortiantur ingressum," meaning "so that they may obtain an easy entry."</note> it is necessary that one **dissolves** them all the more often. For without this <term>Solution</term> <note>The process of liquefying a solid substance, which alchemists believed was the essential first step to purifying it.</note>, this Work cannot be perfectly accomplished, through which, furthermore, the elements are perfectly separated. For this Stone is completed through three elements: **Water**, **Air**, and **Fire**. The **Earth** <note>original: "Terra."</note> is a root and nourishment for the other elements, the true **leaven** <note>original: "Ferment." In the same way yeast makes bread rise, alchemical ferment was believed to "ripen" or transform the base materials into the Stone.</note>. The Water washes, the Air penetrates, and the **Spirit** carries and brings.

Thus, understand now our dissolution: the Spirit or Water cleanses the Stone of all impurity; the Air penetrates even into the root; but the Fire makes the Earth **fixed** and stable. The Water should be given to the thirsty earth in its proper time. The Earth remains fixed in its place, and through it, the three elements are put back together once more. For without the elements, no perfect **tincture** <note>A liquid or medicine capable of transmuting metals or healing the body; the concentrated essence of the Stone.</note> may be prepared. Since, however, in this mixture, the elements are still mixed together quite wildly and disorderly, and lie hidden, no sharp and inner subtlety—which is quite strong in nature and effect—can yet manifest. While the elements are hidden within themselves and lack power, they give off a vapor or smoke, which are notable, sharp **spirits**.

From these roots, Solomon built the **Ark** <note>original: "Archam." This likely refers to the Ark of the Covenant, suggesting that alchemical secrets provided the wealth or wisdom needed for its construction.</note> and adorned the **Temple in Jerusalem**.

In the name of the Most High, take first the highly praised **King**, who is tender, pure, and surrounded by every virtue, and born of the most noble lineage of this world. He wears a crown of the finest and purest gold that may be found in the world, which crown is adorned with three noble gemstones. This King dwells in the **East**, and his power reaches and extends even to the **West**, and his wrath begins from the **South** and terrifies all who dwell in the **North**. <note>The compass points (Orient, Occident, Mittag, Mitternacht) represent the universal influence of the primary alchemical material or the circulation of the spirit through the laboratory apparatus.</note> **Dissolution is the beginning of our Work.** <note>original: "Solutio, nostri Operis initium est."</note> No Tincture is perfect, unless from

### Part One, Treatise I.
b ij

...proceeds from a true and perfect root. <note>original: "vera atque perfecta radice procedat." This phrase concludes the sentence from the previous page regarding the elemental foundation of the Stone.</note> Take this **King**, who wears the beautiful, adorned **Golden Crown** because of his high and rich understanding and his brave spirit; strip him of all his clothing, whatever colors they may be, so that he is entirely naked and pure, free from all the colors of his manifold garments. <note>In alchemy, the "King" often represents Gold or the "Fixed" sulfur. Stripping his clothes refers to removing impurities or surface characteristics of the base metal.</note> Place him in a gently warmed bath, in which his age and nature may rejoice, and see to it that you do not make the bath too hot, lest you burn his tender, pure body, as well as his veins, flesh, and bone. With this same water, rub all his veins gently. Through such soothing and the pleasure of the bath, he will fall asleep. During this sleep of the King, keep the water in a long, mild warmth, so that he remains constantly at one degree of heat. If you now maintain the bath with suitable warmth, the King falls into a deep sleep because of the sweet heat, so that he cannot wake up; through this, he finally becomes so weak that he also dies sweetly of a soft and gentle death. Leave this corpse lying in the warm bath with the same warmth for as long as it takes to complete the **circle of a month** <note>A "circle of a month" likely refers to a full lunar cycle, a common timing mechanism in early laboratory practice.</note>; then for half as long again, yet let the bath cover the dead King on all sides. Then all his powers and bones dissolve, and the King begins to rot, so that his flesh, veins, and bones begin to turn entirely black. <note>This stage is called the **Nigredo** or "blackness." To the alchemist, the turning of the material to black was a successful sign that the substance was "dying" to its old form so it could be reborn as something pure.</note> But his internal heart and internal blood are still beautiful red, fresh, and healthy. <note>The red interior suggests the **Rubedo**, the final "Red" stage of the work, which represents the perfection of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> Thus you have the beginning of the Work, and the death of the King, which is to be understood as our root being turned into water. The Work is carried forward through the suitable heat of the material fire.

I will now further reveal to you concerning the four elements, which are still in a chaotic mixture within the decayed body. Keep your water steadily at the same heat and let the King well <term>putrefy</term> <note>original: "putrificiern." Putrefaction is the process of breaking down a substance through moisture and gentle heat, often compared to the rotting of a seed before it sprouts.</note> through the material fire, maintained and nourished in equal and mild warmth. Then the four elements of the dead body awaken—which is its innermost warmth and natural working power. Once they have awakened in this way, they are divided by the elevation of <term>distillation</term> <note>original: "Distillation." This involves heating the liquid to a vapor and condensing it, effectively separating the "pure" spirit from the "impure" body.</note>, each to its own place.

I will reveal the **Garden of Paradise** to you, so that you may understand the Work all the better, and I will first tell you what the **Tree** in the middle of the garden is.

Secondly, what the **Earth** is in which the Tree is planted.

Thirdly, what the poisonous and cunning **Serpent** is that gave Eve the advice to pluck the apple.

### Fourthly, what the four waters are that flow through the Garden of Paradise.

The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil <note>original: "Boni & Mali"</note> was compared to our **Root**: The **Earth** to our **Mercury** <term>Mercurio: here referring to the "Philosophical Mercury," the fluid medium of the work</term>: In which our Root accomplished its perfect **Tincture** / for it receives our **King**. The poisonous serpent is our **Resolving Water**, <note>original: "hoc eſt, Mercurius in Waſſer reſolutus"</note> *that is, Mercury dissolved into water*. The four rivers that refresh the Tree of Life of our Root / are nothing other / than our **Mercurial Water** / in which our **King** is dissolved / and that same water divides itself / into four main rivers / that encircle the earth. The first water is called **Pison**, which surrounds the whole land of India / in which there is much precious and pure gold. This water signifies our **Mercurial Water** / for it encompasses all of India / in which there is much precious Gold: understand / our **Root** / when it is surrounded by the Mercurial water / then in it is found very pure and precious Indian Gold: Likewise understand / that the main river / and the first divided water called **Pison** is all of the same significance as our Mercurial water. For it is indeed the first main river / from which the first river and water divide / meaning the **Elements**.

The second water is called **Gihon** <note>original: "Gyhon"</note>, which flows around all of Ethiopia <note>original: "Morenland," literally "Land of the Moors"</note> / <note>original: "Æquiparatur aquæ nigredinem inferenti"</note> *It is likened to the water that brings on blackness.* <note>This refers to "Nigredo," the first major stage of alchemy involving putrefaction and decay.</note> The third water is called **Hiddekel** <note>original: "Hideckiel"</note>, which turns / and flows toward the East. This water signifies the **Element of Air** for through the air the seed of the Man and Woman comes forth perfectly. The fourth water is called **Euphrates**, which signifies the **Element of Fire** / and the end of our **Stone**.

When the **King** is turned into a spirit / then simply keep the degree of the **Fire** constant / so he rises up and down <note>This refers to the process of "Circulation," where vapors rise and condense repeatedly in the flask.</note> / until he lays himself down again in the bottom of the glass in a **White** form and color. When you see this / do not hurry too much / give him plenty of room / so that the Work may become all the more perfect / afterward proceed with that same degree of fire <note>original: "ignis uſque ad Rubedinem"</note> *until the Redness* <note>The final stage of the work, "Rubedo."</note>. <note>original: "Niſi ſemen viri cum femine mulieris conjun- gatur, nihil in opere perficies."</note> *Unless the seed of the man is joined with the seed of the woman, you will accomplish nothing in the work.*

There are **four keys** of the Art / the first is **Solution** <note>original: "Solutio"</note> and **Putrefaction** <note>original: "Putrefactio"</note>. The second is **Sublimation** or separation. The third is the perfection of mixing the seed of the Man and Woman with a natural marriage / and to unite entirely and completely with one another. The fourth is the **Seal of Hermes** <note>original: "Sigillum Hermetis"</note>, **Putrefaction** <note>original: "Putrefactio 42. diebus abſolvitur"</note> *is completed in 42 days*: but it would be better for it to be slightly longer / for no harm occurs through this. <note>original: "Præcipua totius Operis cura eſt ne calor nimium intendatur."</note> *The primary care of the whole work is that the heat should not be increased too much.* The **Fire of Putrefaction** <note>original: "Ignis Putrefactionis"</note> should be made from a wick of **feathered alum** <note>original: "Alumnis plumosi," likely referring to asbestos or mineral wool used as a permanent wick in oil lamps.</note>

It concludes by outlining the four "keys" or essential operations of the work: solution, sublimation, union, and the seal of Hermes.</summary>

# TRACTATE II.
## The Little Book of Salomon Trismosin concerning the Red
## Lion and his Treasury.

<margin>B</margin>
Among all arts, the **Subject of the TINCTURE** <term>Tincture: the "Philosopher's Stone" in liquid or powdered form, capable of "tinging" or transforming base metals into gold</term>, that is, the Tincture-like essence, is the highest and most excellent art above all other arts in this world. The eternal Godhead has reserved this for Himself and does not allow it to be revealed to everyone; for He does not wish for all people to be rich, but rather that one person should serve another with friendliness and labor. And although this art was revealed to many pagans, especially to great leaders such as kings, it happened in no other way than this: because they knew nothing of God the Almighty, whether they wished to humble themselves or reflect upon the fact that there must be a God who created such a mystery. Namely, that such a Tincture-like essence can transform <note>original: "tingiren"</note> so much imperfect metal, and shall turn it into the best gold, stable in all high tests, and better gold than can come out of the mountains.

Or it came through special inspiration from the Highest, as happened to the Holy Three Kings, who were also pagans, who had to carry gold, frankincense, and myrrh over a very long journey to the Lord Christ our Savior. But the pagans were very secretive in such arts and kept them hidden, so that others of their kind would not be offended, as indeed it should be. And although such pagan kings had to have people who could also work such arts, it was always done with diligence to ensure those chosen were predestined for it and also secretive; and I say myself that not everyone is qualified for it.

I, Trismosin, have had nine disciples; none was successful except for one, **Philips Hohenheimer** <note>The famous physician and alchemist known as Paracelsus (1493–1541)</note>, a Swiss-born man, a cunning fellow. I say: He will become great in this art; when he reaches his middle age, the world will hear great wonders of him and he will bring many wonders to light. Whoever now [seeks] the great—

<summary>Salomon Trismosin introduces the "Red Lion" tractate, arguing that alchemy is a divine gift reserved for the virtuous and predestined. He notably identifies the famous Paracelsus (Hohenheimer) as his only successful student.</summary>

# OF THE NEW ROSE GARDEN

Whoever is eager to come to the treasure of the **Red Lion** <term>Red Lion: a symbol for the "Philosopher’s Stone" in its final, most potent state, or the fermented "gold" of the chemists</term> must be able to draw the **Suns** <note>original: "Sonnen"; refers to the essence of gold</note> out of the mountains and quench the same in their heat with **Lion's blood**; then the great secret Work shall increase in its strength, so that you will accomplish wonders with it.

You should also be secretive, and set your heart toward God in Heaven with prayer; then your true **Lion** will turn green with the most beautiful blue in the greatest magnificence. For this is the treasure in the world to which nothing is equal, after the eternal; it holds everything within itself: health and wealth, and all-penetrating power. And I tell you, this **Red Lion** tears apart everything that is imperfect and makes it completely perfect again in the highest degree, both in humans and in the **Metals** <note>original: "Metalla"</note>; mark this well. And these gifts are not only despised by the majority, but also greatly abused; for this reason, the eternal God, on account of such ingratitude, does not allow many powerful arts and treasures to be revealed in this world.

## Now follows the Process.

<margin>AB</margin>
Take a strong **Spirit of Wine** <note>original: "Sp. Vini"; high-proof alcohol</note> that has been distilled through seven-fold paper. To one measure of this, pour four **lots** <note>a "lot" is a historical unit of weight, roughly 15-16 grams</note> of <gloss>a special salt</gloss> <note>the asterisk likely indicates sal ammoniac or salt of tartar used to "alcoholize" or sharpen the spirit</note> which has been previously extracted purely in a flask. This Spirit of Wine, alcoholized with <gloss>the salt</gloss> for the purpose of dissolving **Gold**, is to be putrefied, sealed for four days and nights in a very gentle **Mary’s Bath** <term>Mary's Bath: (Balneum Mariae) a water bath used to provide gentle, even heat</term>. Thereafter, distill it again through five-fold Venetian paper; then the Spirit of Wine will be ready for the dissolution.

Thus now begin: Take from Hungary the **fixed Coagulate** <term>Coagulate: a solid substance produced from a liquid; here likely referring to a specific purified gold ore</term>, that is, <margin>Gold</margin> **struck gold** <note>original: "☉ percusum"; gold leaf or hammered gold</note> as it is found at the gold-beaters, eight lots. Put this into a flask and pour the Spirit of Wine upon it so that it covers it well. Set it, well-sealed, into the water bath to putrefy for eight days and nights with very gentle warmth. Then distill the Spirit from it until it reaches an oily consistency, very gently. Thereafter, pour fresh Spirit of Wine upon it—as much as you gently drew off—and for the third time, having poured fresh Spirit of Wine upon the oiliness, let it putrefy for eight days. Then distill **through the side** <note>original: "per latus"; using a retort where the neck extends to the side</note> subtly, and everything will rise over as a spiritual, moist work. Let this rest until it settles. Then the watery part should be subtly poured off, and the material washed several times; then it is ready for **Coagulation** <note>the process of turning a liquid into a solid</note>. The work, now being entirely dry, is placed into a round vial, well-secured with the **Seal of Hermes** <term>Seal of Hermes: an airtight, hermetic seal, often made by melting the glass neck of a flask shut</term> or otherwise with good **lute** <term>Lute: a clay or paste used to seal chemical vessels against heat and pressure</term>. Set it in the "Regiment of Fire" in subtle, sifted ashes, cooked with steady, gentle warmth until it reveals itself as a fixed and incombustible stone, like a **red ruby**. Then you have the **Lion**, entirely beautiful and perfect.

# PART ONE, TREATISE II.
# THE RED LION.

<margin>N3</margin>
Regarding this **Red Lion**, grind it to the smallest and most subtle powder, and **putrefy** <note>to break down or rot the material to release its inner essence</note> it again with the upper water of the **Spirit of Wine** <note>original: "Sp. Vini"; high-proof alcohol</note>, as before; however, renew it every five days with fresh [spirit]. This should be done for the third time with fresh Spirit of Wine, so that it is converted into the volatile **spiritual essence** <note>original: "Geistlichkeit"</note>. And when the Spirit of Wine is drawn off in a **water bath** <note>original: "Mariæ B." for *Balneum Mariae*; a gentle double-boiler method</note> until it reaches an oily consistency, there remains a blood-red **liquid** <note>original: "Liquor"</note>; this is called the **Blood of the Red Lion**. This is now the greatest and most powerful treasure of the whole world, to which nothing is equal.

### FERMENTATION
### OF THE RED LION.

Now pay attention to the tincturing nature of the **Red Lion**. Take **Hungarian leaf gold** <note>original: "Ungerisch Blattgold"</note>, finely ground for three hours on a smooth **marble** <note>original: "Marmol"</note>; take four **lots** <note>a historical weight unit, approx. 15-16 grams</note>. After grinding, place it into a glass vessel specifically suited for this purpose, which is sized for four lots—neither too small nor too large. Place it in sifted **ashes** <note>original: "gesegte äschen"; an ash-bath used for uniform heating</note> with gentle heat. Pour the **Blood of the Red Lion** over it, prepared as described above, so that it covers the gold by the height of a **straw** when laid sideways. Leave the glass open with its **alembic head** <note>original: "Helm"; the cap of the distilling vessel</note>; moisture will still be visible within the glass of the alembic head. Maintain a gentle fire until no more moisture is seen and everything has become dry. Afterward, **seal the glass** <note>original: "versigillier"; hermetically sealing the vessel for the final heating</note> at the neck and place the glass, along with the matter, back into the subtle ashes so that it is half-buried. Apply a subtle fire beneath it, so that the glass is as hot as the sun shines during the **Dog Days** <note>original: "Hundstagen"; the hottest days of mid-to-late summer</note>. Let it stand in this heat until the matter begins to turn blackish; then maintain it at the same heat until the blackness gradually fades. Then you shall strengthen the fire to half-heat, yet in such a way that nothing rises from the matter; you must take great care of this. Then many kinds of beautiful colors will reveal themselves.

Now you shall govern the fire from degree to degree so wisely until you arrive at white-gray, and finally at pure white; thus this treasure has become entirely **fixed** <note>chemically stable and resistant to change by fire</note> and incombustible. Now maintain the fire at a high heat, and it will begin to turn yellow, and finally, with great wonder, it will attain the highest, most excellent **Salamandrine redness** <term>Salamandrine redness: a deep, permanent red color, named after the mythical salamander that lived in fire, signifying the final stage and perfection of the Philosopher’s Stone</term>. And thus this Work is brought to its conclusion, and thereafter requires no further labor other than to **tincture** <term>tincture: the process of projecting the Stone onto a base metal to transform it into gold, or onto a body to heal it</term> with it, as follows.

# Note the preparation of the Red Lion; proceed in this way:

<margin>Note well.</margin> **T**ake one part of this work, finely ground, and let a thousand parts of the best Hungarian Gold melt; cast this part into the flow and let it remain in the melt for three and a half hours <note>original: "vierdthalb stund"</note>. This part transforms the Gold into pure <term>Tincture|a potent medicinal or alchemical substance capable of transforming base metals or healing the body</term>. After this, cast one part [of this Tincture] onto a thousand parts of Silver in the melt; it transforms it all into the highest Gold, as malleable as lead <note>original: "Hämmerreich als ein Bley"; meaning the gold is exceptionally pure and soft enough to be worked easily</note>, excellent in all tests.

From this <term>Tincture|a potent medicinal or alchemical substance capable of transforming base metals</term>, also take one part and cast it upon a thousand parts of <term>Mercury|also known as quicksilver</term> that comes from the mountains in the fire; thus it becomes pure <term>Tincture|a potent medicinal or alchemical substance capable of transforming base metals</term>. From this, take another part and cast it upon a thousand parts of raw mountain <term>Mercury|also known as quicksilver</term>; thus it transforms it once more into pure <term>Tincture|a potent medicinal or alchemical substance capable of transforming base metals</term>: it all remains a powder. Take one part of this <term>Tincture|a potent medicinal or alchemical substance capable of transforming base metals</term> and cast it upon a thousand parts of mountain <term>Mercury|also known as quicksilver</term> when it smokes in the crucible; thus the highest and best Gold is made, stable in all tests. In this way, <term>projection|the final stage of the alchemical work, where the "Stone" or Tincture is cast upon base metals to transmute them</term> is also performed upon Copper <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, Tin <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, and Lead <note>original symbol: ♄</note>.

Thus you see the great wonders of God, and what secrets He has placed into His creatures, especially into Gold, which is the highest among the seven <note>referring to the seven metals of antiquity associated with the seven planets</note> and is called the Royal Metal by all <term>Philosophers|the historical term for alchemists and natural scientists</term>.

Within it lies the great treasure of kings, if it is brought into its spiritual state <note>original: "Geistlichkeit"; referring to the volatile or essence-form of the metal</note>, leading to wealth and long life in this world. # Now follows the Augmentation of the Red Lion.

**Y**ou should know that if you take the first Red Lion—which you have cooked to fixity <note>the state where a substance no longer evaporates or changes when heated</note> with its own red blood—and draw it back again into a spiritual state, and then make it fixed again for a short time, it will tinge three thousand times more with one part than it did before. And where it is dissolved again and cooked to its perfection, it tinges all metals six times more with one part, and after the solution, it doubles by six. And the <term>Multiplication|the process of increasing the quantity or the transmuting power of the alchemical Stone</term> is beyond words.

# TINCTURE II.

## Now follows a tincture of the Black Eagle of Salomon Trismosin.

This **TINCTURE** was described by a Philosopher named Pitromofon <note>This name may be a corruption or pseudonym typical of alchemical literature, possibly referring to a specific monastic author</note>, concerning the Black Eagle: From Antimony. He sought for many years in Chemistry <note>original: "Chymia"</note> and wished to make the tincture from many various things, but nothing revealed itself; only in one single thing is the Subject <term>Subjectum|The "starting material" or "prime matter" from which the alchemist begins their work</term> hidden with its Colors. Whoever wishes to go to work with these matters must read all the Philosophers and diligently behold and look through their described tinctures; thus it will be found that all Philosophers speak of only one single thing or essence. And although one Philosopher has a shorter path than the other, they nevertheless use only a single essence in this Art, and without that same thing, no tincture is produced, as is evident; and everyone should well weigh this saying (as follows):

->In the Higher Sphere<-
->There is in the Middle of the Forehead<-
->A Vein, which is the First Rule<-
->Of the PHILOSOPHERS.<-

And whoever understands this saying will learn what the Subject refers to.

In the Black Eagle—that is **Antimony** <term>Antimonium|A brittle, silvery-gray metalloid. In alchemy, it was symbolized by the wolf or the eagle because of its "voracious" ability to purify gold by consuming other metals</term>—a black glittering stone in appearance, white on the inside, and of a great redness, much gold is to be found therein; and whoever can also separate it through Art from the black Antimony into the eagle, he has his nourishment to sustain himself; and it is called Dark Gold <note>original: "Aurum obscurum"</note>. ## AUGMENTATION

Now take one ounce of **Gold Leaf** <term>Aurum foliatum|Gold that has been hammered into extremely thin sheets for easier dissolution</term> from the goldsmiths; add this to the **Astral Eagle** <note>The "Astral Eagle" is a poetic term for the highly distilled, volatile solvent prepared in the previous paragraph</note> and seal it with the **Seal of Hermes** <term>Sigillo Hermetis|An airtight, hermetic seal, typically made by melting the glass neck of a vessel shut</term>. The **first color** will appear in the neck of the glass as a mixed redness. In the **sixth, seventh, and eighth** transformations, according to the **Regimen of the Fire** <term>Regiment des Fewers|The systematic control of heat levels in an alchemical process</term>, the blackness disappears and becomes **Blue** and **Red** with streaks, as if they were worms; afterward, one sees **Yellow** and also **Green** streaks. In the **ninth, tenth, and eleventh** transformations, by the Regimen of the Fire, the neck of the glass becomes black at the top, and within it appear **Red, Yellow, Green, and White** droplets.

The most noble Master Craftsman <note>original: "Werckmeister"; referring to God as the divine architect</note> has ordered and arranged things so that in this elemental world, the affairs and trades of men—together with his bodily brother, the Sun—follow a wonderful order of changes, just as the two great lights in the heavens were created at the beginning of the world: one for the day, and the other for the night.

Since, however, according to the opinion and meaning of all wise philosophers, the earthly Moon <note>original: "☽" (Luna), representing the metal Silver</note> lacks fixation <note>original: "fixion"; the alchemical property of being stable in fire and not evaporating</note>, I have revealed something hidden and secret from the innermost mysteries of philosophy to the son of wisdom <note>original: "filio sapientiæ"; a traditional term for a student of the alchemical arts</note>. This is so that the Silver Sun <note>Silver, which alchemists viewed as an "imperfect" or "night-time" version of gold</note>—which has long traveled upon two red wheels—may finally be raised to the high level of her brother’s [the Sun’s] status, so that she no longer presides over the night, but rather over the day, shining over our world with a golden luster. I am also of the opinion that those who have spent much effort trying to coagulate Mercury <note>original: "Mercurio"; attempting to turn liquid quicksilver into a solid</note> have acted quite foolishly, since they already have the Moon [Silver] almost fixed, which they could very easily bring to a higher nature. By such means, Venus <note>original: "♀"; the metal Copper</note> and Saturn <note>original: "♄"; the metal Lead</note> can also be made into the Sun <note>original: "☉"; Gold</note>. Although the philosophers have primarily philosophized about the Moon and her defects, the Moon lacks weight; this weight will be abundantly given to you by Saturn, who is closest to the Sun [Gold] in weight. For this reason, philosophers commonly lose the leprous gold <note>original: "Aussetzige Gold"; a term for base metals that look like gold but are chemically "unclean" or unstable</note>.

The philosophers and astronomers attribute the Earth of the world to Saturn. Now, what is heavier than the Earth? What is weightier? Therefore, in the heavens, Saturn completes his circle in thirty years because of his great weight.

The Moon also lacks fixation—that is, the complete ripening or "decoction." Fiery Mars <note>original: "♂"; the metal Iron</note> will share this with you in abundance, as fixation is primarily attributed to him—partly because he is most like the heat of the Sun, and partly because he is least consumed by the fire among us. However, color is very easily increased by the indivisible Venus, the companion of the Sun, whom the natural magicians <note>original: "Magi naturales"; scholars who studied the hidden powers within nature</note> acknowledge to be a goddess of beautiful color. Nevertheless, we attribute color and weight to Mars according to the philosophers, in whom you might enclose the fixation. But how these three bodies [Saturn, Mars, Venus] are to be proportioned and mixed with one another, you must perform partly through astronomy and partly through the investigation of nature—astronomically regarding their distances or spans, and also regarding their proximity to the Moon.

...its destructibility is entirely consumed, and until the pure part within the <term>Venus</term> <note>Alchemical name for Copper</note> is turned into running <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note>. God be blessed, praised, and exalted above all, who has revealed to us the blessed water and its power <note>original: "Tugendt"; referring to the inherent medicinal or transformative properties</note> which is hidden from the many. For its power is wonderful and surpasses all other virtues; it is powerful enough to separate the pure from the impure within the <term>bodies</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, making the body <term>subtle</term> <note>Refined or volatile</note> and bringing it back to its <term>first matter</term> <note>original: "ersten Materi"; the primal, undifferentiated state of substance</note>. And when it reaches that state, it causes the imperfect and the perfect bodies to unite in their smallest parts, which it cleanses at the same time, binding them into a constant and inseparable bond.

Nor should anyone wonder why the perfect body <note>Gold or silver</note> must be mixed in there. For the imperfect <term>body</term> <note>the purified copper</note>, though cleansed in the manner mentioned above, is nonetheless currently without a soul and cannot live unless its soul is given back to it. But the perfect body *is* its soul; therefore, the soul must be given to it and be unified with it. But then it lives and rejoices with the soul for all eternity.

# TREATISE IV.
## Containing Several Secrets of Phil. Theophrastus Paracelsus, **CONCERNING THE PHILOSOPHER’S STONE.**

->A Writing<-

# OF THEOPHRASTUS

->On the<-

## Reduction of Metals into their First Matter, To Doctor Poldörffern.

->Also:<-

### By the Same: Fixation upon the Mercury of Saturn.

->This rule was written by **Theophrastus** to **Doctor Poldörffern**, Professor at Levoča <note>original: "Lereckaw"</note>, from Bratislava <note>original: "Preßburg"</note>, who was formerly his traveling companion.<-

You wish to know from me that which you yourself could well conclude—namely, how metals might be transformed according to the ancient process and brought into one another's **matter** <note>original: "Matery"</note>. But that I should send such a secret to you upon your request on a piece of paper through this wicked world—you will not teach me (nor other ignorant ones with your <term>High Schools</term> <note>A dismissive reference to the established academic universities of the era, which Paracelsus famously rejected</note>) to write such things to you plainly. Yet, on account of the faithful service you have rendered me, I send this to you to fulfill your request; and it is this: you must first know that the metals must be brought back into their first and last <term>essence</term> <note>original: "wesen"</note>, otherwise all your toil and labor is for nothing, useless, and in vain. Thus you can then cleanse them of their impurity, and the mother can [be separated] from her

# NEW ROSARY.

The Bridegroom, whom the ancients called the **Sulfur of the Philosophers** and the **Father**, receives the second **coagulation** <note>The process of thickening or solidifying a liquid substance</note> through the addition of their Salt and Spirit; it then becomes a higher and better metal than it was before. Thus, the final creation is accomplished, and it is possible for nature—following the process of **Silver, Gold, Copper, Iron, Lead, and Tin** <note>original symbols: ☾, ☉, ♀, ♂, ♄, ♃</note>—to truly and justly be transformed into **Gold**.

And so the beginning and end of the world is rightly understood and accomplished according to the process of the ancients. However, this is not granted to everyone, but only to those to whom God wishes to reveal it out of a special spirit as a gift of Grace through His mercy.

And you should know that there is no other or more direct way known to us to bring the metals back into their <term>Mercury</term> <note>The "living" or fluid state of a metal, considered its primary matter</note> than what we have set down in our booklet <term>on Putrefaction</term> <note>original: "de Putrefactione"; the stage of alchemical decay or breaking down</note> regarding four salts. In this way, you have the metal "living," like any other <term>Mercury</term>, and the <term>Eagle</term> thus becomes "flying."

It is then called the <term>Borax of the Philosophers</term>, which we write about in the booklet <term>on the Virtue of Vitriol</term> <note>original: "de Virtute Vitrioli"</note>. Within this Borax, the <term>Flying Eagle</term> has hidden itself with its feathers—which are the spirits.

Now take the "lime" <note>calx or powdered oxide</note> of whichever metal you wish from the <term>Strong Water</term> <note>original: "Aq. Fort" (Aqua Fortis); nitric acid</note>, as much as you like, and add half as much of the <term>Flying Eagle</term> as there is metal. Then place it in a coated glass flask, set it in sand, and <term>sublime</term> <note>Heat a solid until it turns to vapor and collects again at the top of the vessel</note> it upward. Everything will rise together, no matter which metal it may be.

Vini"; high-proof alcohol</note>, and not just "burning wine" <note>original: "Vinum ardens"; likely a lower-proof brandy</note>, so that it stands at least six fingers high / over the Gold in a delicate flask or vial, proportional to the amount of Gold / set it to <term>putrefy</term> for at least one month in a hot <term>Maria’s Bath</term> <note>original: "Mar. Bal."; a water bath or bain-marie</note> / thus the color of the Gold enters the Spirit of Wine / pour that off into a separate glass / and you may, for greater yield, pour Spirit of Wine over it a second time / and also a third time / until you have drawn all the color out of the Gold / and the Body of the Gold <note>original: "Corpus Solis"</note> remains white through the aforementioned process / then separate the Spirit of Wine from the <term>Form</term> <note>The essential medicinal essence</note> of the Gold over a gentle fire or steam bath / and use it as shown in the administration. # Letters of Mr. Wilhelm Bombast von Hohenheim /
### Doctor of Medicine <note>original: "Medicinæ D."</note> To his son Philippus
### THEOPHRASTUS.

Dear son Philippus / know that through divine grace we have encountered a true <term>Particular Tincture</term> <note>An alchemical substance capable of transmuting a specific quantity of base metal into gold, though less powerful than the "Universal" Philosopher’s Stone</note> / which I herewith faithfully describe to you: I wish / God knows / that you were here with me / for without my presence you will not be able to achieve such a beginning / because it requires a special / and thereafter complete skill to discover its nature / otherwise it is not possible to proceed without this mediator. Therefore, set out at once / so that I may perceive from your words / what your judgment of this may be: especially because I do not know / whether you are in Ohmberg or not / for such fellows are not to be entrusted with letters / for which you will rightly not blame me. However, if I receive your reply / and learn of your situation / I will speak further with you / regarding what my intention is / through writings.

### Thereupon follows the process thus:

Take three parts of Antimony, one part of Gold <note>symbol: ☉; Sol</note> / nine parts of <term>sublimated mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurij sublimati"; mercury chloride, a highly toxic white crystalline powder used as a reagent</note>. Mix these three pieces together / and grind them very finely together / and distill it with its appropriate medium <term>via Retort</term> five times / always pouring it back over <note>a process called cohobation</note> / until it is transformed into a perfect Oil. Afterward, one must distill a very good <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: "Sp. Vini"; concentrated ethanol/alcohol</note> from it also five times <term>via water-bath</term> <note>original: "per Balneum"; a vessel of hot water used to ensure gentle, even heating</note> / thus the Oil becomes fixed, which then coagulates / that transforms 1 part into 15 parts of Mercury into good Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note>. Herewith you have the entire process / as I have now made it for the third time / let this be commended to you by me / although I know / that you do not easily cast pearls before swine / I commend you to God to serve you.

# THE INCREASE OF GOLD.
## BY THEOPHRASTUS.

### To obtain a great treasure in a short time.

Go away into the mountains / called the Caspian Mountains <note>Montes Caspij; historically associated in legend with the lost tribes of Israel</note>, in which mountains the Jews / who are called the Red Jews <note>A mythological concept in medieval German folklore, here used as an alchemical allegory for a specific mineral or "impure" ore that contains gold</note> / who were enclosed by the great Alexander, reside. These Jews nourish themselves solely with the very best Gold / and therefore their sweat is very precious. Take of these Jews / the very fattest and thickest / as many as you wish / namely a hundred or two. For a hundred Jews give you four loth <note>a unit of weight, roughly 2 ounces total</note> of <term>Gold</term> <note>symbol: ☉; Sol</note> at one time. Lead these Jews into a warm bath / which is called the Dry-Water <note>original: "trucken-Wasser"; likely a term for mercury or a specific chemical solvent that does not "wet" things like normal water</note> / the same lies outside the mountains / and wash the same Jews well with this water / and rub their skin / until it becomes white. Thereafter prepare a warm water in a triangular vessel / until it begins to smoke / then the water is warm enough / then let the Jews go into it / and let them stand therein for the length of an *Ave Maria* <note>The time it takes to recite the prayer; a common way to measure time in early modern recipes</note> / thereafter pour the bathwater out with the Jews / into another simple vat / and scrub them with hands or brushes / until they become quite White / and the sweat shall be well drawn out by that same water / and washed off / and the skin made quite thin / this happens to some Jews once / to some twice / to some three times with the washing in the warm water bath. And note / when these Jews are thus thin and sent out or rubbed down / then wipe the bathwater off them—

each one has taken a shorter and closer path: Some have come to a good end, but some have accomplished nothing. For a good beginning brings forth a good end; let that be well said to you.

When Nature has ceased in the work, therewith let the Artist begin to work. For as already reported, the spirit of our Material works, destroys, and breaks the metallic essence: This spirit dwells in all elements and is full of smoke and wind, yet cold and fiery: It is recognized by few and considered of little value: It is a bitter juice, and yet has the greatest sweetness hidden within it; that is the *Soul of Azoth* <note>original: "Anima Azothi"</note>.

# A BRIEF ADMONITION to the True-Hearted Reader.

Much-beloved, Christian-zealous reader, and lover of heavenly truth and the Chemical Study <note>original: Studii Chymici</note>; since the following chapter or little treatise of our highly enlightened, noble, and dear teacher <term>Præceptor; a formal title for a respected instructor or master</term> **THEOPHRASTUS** <note>referring to Paracelsus</note>, concerning his **Tincture of the Physicians** <term>Tinctura Physicorum; a legendary alchemical medicine believed to cure all diseases and transmute metals</term>, has come to me—of which he has given a thorough and true report, which is in many places much better and more extensively composed than can be found in his printed volumes—I have therefore wished to arrange it here for your benefit. I do this so that you may perceive and recognize my true, heartfelt mind toward all lovers of dear Alchemy <note>original: Alchymey</note> in this work, and see that I am inclined to faithfully promote their most honorable purpose <note>original: honestiss. propositum</note>. Included is a fine explanation <term>declaration; a clarifying exposition</term> of the four Secrets of Paracelsus <term>Arcana Paracelsi; the "arcana" were the hidden "star-like" virtues or essential powers of a substance</term>, namely: 1. The Secret of the First Matter <note>original: Arcanum primæ materiæ</note>. 2. Of the Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: Lapidis Philosophorum</note>. 3. Of the Mercury of Life <note>original: Mercurii vitæ</note>. 4. Concerning his Tincture <note>original: Tincturam</note>. I obtained these in Tyrol from the high and well-born Lord, Mr. Maximilian von und zu Baumgarten, Baron of Hohen Schwangau and Erbach, Hereditary Marshal of the Noble Prince-Bishopric of our Dear Lady’s Cathedral in Augsburg, Count Palatine of the Lateran and the Empire <note>original: Comite Palatino Lateranensi & Cæsaeo</note>, etc., my gracious Lord and benevolent patron <term>Mecœnate; a patron of the arts or sciences, after the Roman Maecenas</term>, as well as a highly experienced Chemist <note>original: Chymico</note>. May you receive and understand this from me in the best way and apply it to your own benefit; that is my heartfelt wish for everyone. Farewell, etc.

### There follows the Preparation or Making of Antimony <note>original symbol: ♁</note>.

Take a good, strong crucible, and place into it four pounds of Antimony. Let it start in the forge by itself, well-covered. Blow upon it until it flows well. Alongside this, take a good core-steel <note>high-quality steel</note>, have it beaten into a thin plate, and let it cool, so that it shatters like glass. Of this Iron <note>original symbol: ♂</note> plate, take one pound; let it first glow red-hot and put it immediately into the melted Antimony <note>original symbol: ♁</note>. Cover it again and heap coals over it. Let it flow well by blowing upon it, and stir the materials together with a cold iron rod so that nothing coarse is found anymore in the crucible, until everything in the crucible becomes like water. Then pour it quickly into a cold mortar that has been slightly greased; let it cool by itself. When all this has been pounded together, sieve it into a powder and keep it until you have need of it.

This is, and is called, our Alcohol <term>Alcool; in early alchemy, this referred to an extremely fine, impalpable powder, not a liquid</term>, Magnesia, Mercury of Life <note>original: Mercurius vitæ</note>, or the way to make the Quintessence <term>Quinta Essentia; the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual core of a substance</term>. This aforementioned Alcohol, Magnesia, or Mercury of Life, or Mercurial water, which has been previously purified, as you well—

Take of the First Matter in a flask <note>original: flaccum</note>: as if he were to say, the Regulus of Antimony <term>Regulus of Antimony: the metallic heart or "little king" produced by smelting antimony ore</term>, let it be dissolved in *Aqua Regis* <term>Aqua Regis: "Royal Water," a potent mixture of acids used to dissolve noble metals</term>, and place it in dung for putrefaction <note>Placing a vessel in warm horse dung was a common way to maintain a steady, gentle heat for decomposition</note>. By "Monarchy" we understand in this place common Sal Ammoniac <term>Sal Ammoniac: ammonium chloride, used to "spiritualize" or volatilize solids</term>, and by distilling it thus you will have our common Mercury, which you shall turn into water. Read more clearly about this Secret in Theophrastus <note>The famous alchemist Paracelsus</note> *On Long Life*, book 3, chapter 6, and in the *Apocalypse of Hermes*, concerning the second essence: for what is lacking in one place / is restored in another.

## II. THE SECRET.
<note>original: II. ARCANVM</note>
## THE PHILOSOPHER’S STONE.

Take the Element of Mercury, and separate the pure from the impure, let the same then reverberate <term>Reverberate: to heat a substance in a furnace where the flame is reflected back down onto the material</term> until it reaches whiteness, sublimate this only through Sal Ammoniac until it resolves again / thereafter place it in a Pelican <term>Pelican: a special glass vessel with two "arms" that allow condensed vapors to flow back into the main body, facilitating continuous circulation</term> / let it digest for a month / then coagulate it into a Body; this will burn no more / and consume itself no more / remaining incorruptible / the bodies through which it passes / are made permanent through the cementing process.

### Declaration of the Philosopher’s Stone.

Take the Element of Mercury, and separate the pure from the impure. That is: Take our matter, and place it in its seed <note>original: sperma</note>, and use the Stibium <term>Stibium: another name for antimony</term>, thereafter let it reverberate into whiteness: as if to say, thus another Regulus comes from it / calcine that / (it teaches how to make from this common Mercury the Mercury of the Philosophers or the ferment, and resolve it again) when after this the two seeds—that is, common Mercury and the Mercury of the Philosophers—are married together / then they resolve themselves in a triple vessel and a vaporous fire. Thereafter place it in a Pelican / let it digest for a month / then coagulate it into a Body) this is all spoken in the Cabalistic manner <note>meaning coded or symbolic alchemical language</note>, as if he wished to say: when you have let your two seeds dissolve in the triple vessel and vaporous fire: then let it stand so long until the whiteness or redness comes / then the Stone is ready.

Theophrastus <note>The famous Swiss-German physician and alchemist Paracelsus</note> describes this process in the sacred book *On Long Life* <note>original: *de Vita longa*</note>. In Book 3, Chapter 6, he most clearly names the material of our Stone and teaches what should be taken from the material, or how it should be cleansed of superfluities, which he also does in his *Manual*. Take immature mineral electrum, place it in its "seed" <note>original: *Sperma*</note> to wash away the filth, and purify it to the highest degree you can using antimony <note>original: *Stibium*</note> according to alchemical practice, so that you suffer no harm from its unruly nature. And there follows the method of making Mercury. Immature mineral electrum is our matter, as it is found in the shops <note>likely referring to apothecary or merchant stalls</note>. The "seed" <note>original: *Sperma*</note> is nothing other than saltpeter. By "antimony" <note>original: *Stibium*</note>, understand ground charcoal powder <note>The author provides a common alchemical "key" where one substance name actually refers to another to keep secrets from the uninitiated</note>. Therefore, proceed thus: Take one pound of our matter and a quarter-pound of the "seed," mix them together, let it gently come to a flow, and throw more in. Do this for about three hours, always stirring with a piece of wood when you throw it in; then pour it into a casting cone <term>Gießbuckel: a conical mold used to separate the purified metal (regulus) from the slag</term>, and you will find a well-purified Regulus <term>Regulus: the metallic button or mass that settles at the bottom of a crucible; here specifically the "Regulus of Antimony"</term>, suitable not only for medicine but also for the Stone or the Universal work. And if our Matter is not purged and purified in this way, it is not useful because of its impurity, which is entirely removed by this process. Theophrastus, in the place mentioned above, calls this purged Regulus a "form marked in another place." King Solomon calls it the *Stellio* <note>Latin for a spotted lizard; used here because of the "star" pattern that appears on the metal's surface</note>. The poet Palingenius calls it the Arcadian boy, the Arcadian, and so on. And all this is because a star appears during the melting <note>When antimony is highly purified, a crystalline pattern resembling a star forms on the surface as it cools</note>. **Note Well:** Let it flow once more with saltpeter alone for a good quarter of an hour; the star will be more beautiful. However, it is unnecessary for our work.

### Process of Medicine.

Our Regulus must be turned into running Mercury, and this Mercury into Water; give four grains weight of this to the patient, as Theophrastus taught in his book mentioned above; thus the medicine is ready. Theophrastus teaches in the book *Treasure of Treasures* how to clean this Matter of ours, except he leaves out the antimony: the "rainwater" is nothing other than the "seed" <note>saltpeter</note>, the cinnabar <note>original: *Zinober*</note> is our Matter, and there follows a most beautiful process to make our Mercury from our purged matter, suitable for the universal path as well as for this medicine.

### To make common Mercury.

Make a three-part vessel; pour the Mercury through the small tube into the first part, so that it runs through the middle and the third into the receiver <note>original: *Recipienten*; the vessel intended to collect the distilled product</note> like water.

# CONCERNING ANTIMONY BY ALEXANDER von Süchten.

### What is Antimony?

It is a mineral created by God from a metallic matter; that is, from <term>Quick-silver</term> <note>original: *Argento Vivo*</note> that has been cooked with **Sulfur** in the **bowels of the earth** <note>original: *visceribus terræ*</note>.

### Since metals are also made of Mercury and Sulfur, will they not be the same thing?

the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: *Argentum Vivum*</note> of Antimony and that of the metals are indeed one and the same matter. However, the **Form**—such as the **Sulfur of Antimony**—is not metallic, but rather mineral. It is a type of Sulfur that can be altered through **digestion** <note>a process of slow, constant heating</note> and brought to a state of purity that the sulfur of other metals cannot reach. Therefore, Antimony is an imperfect metal and is called <term>Saturn</term> <note>In alchemy, Saturn usually refers to lead, but here describes antimony's heavy, dark, and "unripe" state</note> in Philosophy.

### What is one to expect from Antimony?

The **highest Medicine**, the like of which the world cannot produce, and that which all the Sages from the beginning of the world have sought.

### But how does one obtain this from it?

Through great toil and labor, and above all through the **Grace of GOD**.

### How does this happen?

First, a **Mercury** must be separated from it in the manner—

<header>Part One, Tract IV.</header>

Just as the miner separates **Antimony** from the ore in which it grew, he must do so with such caution that the **metallic luster** <note>original: *Metallische schein*</note> seen in the Antimony is not burned away or driven out by the fire. Instead, it should be extracted higher and better. This metallic form must remain until it reaches the **whiteness of silver**. At that point, it is in its highest degree; as soon as the slag is removed from it, it appears not as Antimony anymore, but as the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Mercurius Philosophorum*</note>. It allows itself to be poured like any other metal and flows like a pure **quicksilver** <note>original: *Quecksilber*</note>; these are its signs.

### What then is the great significance of this luster?

For the metallic form is a **living fire** that accomplishes everything that must happen in this work, until the very end of the <term>Digestion</term> <note>The process of subjecting a substance to gentle, continuous heat to mature or "ripen" it</note>. This fire is its life, through which the <term>Materia</term> <note>The physical matter or "body" of the substance</note> in which it dwells is purified of all uncleanness. This same fire is the life of the material and of all metals; when this **Form** <note>In alchemy, the "form" is the spiritual or essential quality that gives a substance its identity</note> departs, they no longer live.

### What is removed during the separation that might be harmful?

The remaining mineral moistures and **earthy sulfur**, which increased the poison within the Mercury.

### What kind of Mercury is this then?

It is nothing other than a <term>Quicksilver</term> <note>original: *Argentum Vivum*</note> to which a **mineral sulfur** is attached; this is a pure sulfur, though raw and incomplete. But when it is digested and brought to its perfection, it becomes the <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: *Arcanum*; a "secret" or powerful medicinal essence</note> that <term>tinges</term> <note>Transmutes or dyes the inner nature of a substance</note> and transmutes its Quicksilver from a poisonous state into the **noblest medicine**, the likes of which the world cannot produce.

Regarding this, diligently examine further the *Introductory Mysteries* <note>original: *Mysteria proemina*</note> of Antimony by our philosopher **A.V.S.** <note>Alexander von Süchten</note> and the *Triumphal Chariot* <note>original: *Triumphwagen*; referring to the famous alchemical text *The Triumphal Chariot of Antimony*</note> by **Frater Basilius** <note>Basilius Valentinus, a legendary 15th-century alchemist</note>.

## LITTLE TREATISE <note>original: *Tractatulus*</note>
### A New Rhythmic Verse on the Philosopher’s Stone.

We walked a very difficult road,
Toward a hut that stood open;
Beneath it sat an **Old Gentleman**,
Walking with a staff, most honorable,
Toward us; he offered us both his hand:
"Be welcome by God in this land:
What do you seek here? What is your will?
Tell me that, so that I may fulfill it."
I spoke: "If only we were out of the forest!
We have already walked many various paths;
We seek here the **wealth of the Sages** <note>The "good of the Wise" usually refers to the Philosopher's Stone or the hidden knowledge of alchemy</note>,
Perhaps you have it in your keeping;
So let us both see it also."
The Old Man said: "Just keep traveling further,
And go away from my door;
Follow this road straight ahead."
I spoke: "Oh, you unfaithful man!
Can you show us nothing at all?
And yet you acted just now
As if you wanted to give us the whole world.
Now I have been wandering here many years,
But as often as I come to someone,
He does not let me go quite so empty,
But gives me something to understand,
Even if it is still hidden from me;
But you are completely full of unfaithfulness.
We beg you from our hearts,
Do not let us go from you so empty."

I will tell you what I mean:
When you pay heed to **Nature** alone,

Now you are right, without any mockery;

### ANOTHER <note>original: "ALIVD"</note>

Three things, without which nothing can endure,
If you wish to walk the proper path.
See that you obtain these,
Which will show you a **Stone** <term>Stone: The Philosopher's Stone (Lapis Philosophorum), the legendary goal of alchemy said to transform base metals into gold and provide the Elixir of Life.</term>;
Whoever keeps the same with him
Can truly speak of great wonders:
For he then emerges quickly and soon
Without me out of the wild forest.
And the tender names of these three things
Are divided, and yet are entirely of one nature:
**Spirit, soul, and body** <note>original: "Spiritus, anima & Corpus"</note>,
None of which must be divided from the others.
If you take heed of these three,
Then what is produced will have permanence:
Just as heavenly things—Hope, Love, and Faith—
One without the others is dead and deaf.
In the same way, nothing earthly can endure;
It must have **Soul, Spirit, and Body** <note>original: "Seel, Geist, und Corpus"</note>.
When I had finished reading this as well,
I knew not what else in the world
Could be a thing
That springs from those same three,
And returns again into one,
And that there is no other besides this.

Each of which had only one gate.
She said to me: “Look here and take note;
Within this lies the **Work of all Sages**.” <term>Work of the Sages: Also known as the "Great Work" (Magnum Opus), this refers to the alchemical process of creating the Philosopher's Stone and achieving spiritual perfection.</term>

The four cities could not be understood
If the three were not so dark;

Seven cities and seven metals <note>In alchemy, the seven metals correspond to the seven planetary bodies: Gold (Sun), Silver (Moon), Mercury (Mercury), Copper (Venus), Iron (Mars), Tin (Jupiter), and Lead (Saturn).</note>,

Seven letters and seven words,
Also seven times and seven places;

I spoke to the Maiden again:

Tell me something more here,
How this may be better understood.”
But she withdrew away from me;
I set out after her on the path.
As I followed her so closely,
She soon began to speak:
“Ten letters are set:
One after five, a thousand at the last.”

<header>THE NEW ROSARY <note>original Latin: "ROSARII NOVI"</note></header>

## First Response. <note>original Latin: "Responſio Prima"</note>

A point that moves swiftly in the circle,
Wherein quadrant and triangle stand; <note>In alchemy, the circle, square (quadrant), and triangle are geometric symbols representing the progression from unity to the four elements, then to the three principles (Salt, Sulfur, Mercury), returning finally to the unified Philosopher's Stone.</note>
If you obtain this point, you have it all,
And escape from poverty, need, and danger.

## Q U E S T I O N  II. <note>original Latin: "Q V E S T I O II"</note>

Out of four I am; their war kills me, <note>The "four" refers to the four elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water. Their "war" refers to their opposing qualities (hot/cold, wet/dry) which cause corruption and decay.</note>
Oh, if I could reconcile this war,
Then my soul would not depart from me;
Their war destroys the green grass;
Now, dear counsel, what is that?

## Second Response. <note>original Latin: "Responſio Secunda"</note>

If you want to reconcile the evil four,
So that they do not part from one another,
In fire’s need, make the three into fire; <note>Likely referring to the Three Principles (Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt) being purified through heat.</note>
Then you have a treasure so dear,
That Charles of Ghent <note>Referring to the Holy Roman Emperor Charles V (1500–1558), who was born in Ghent and was one of the wealthiest and most powerful rulers of the era.</note> could not pay for it,
Even though he was a wealthy man.

## Q U E S T I O N  III. <note>original Latin: "Q V E S T I O III"</note>

Before there were four; now there are only three;
Preserve the fifth; <note>The "fifth" is the Quintessence (literally "fifth essence"), the pure, incorruptible core of a substance.</note> now set the fourth free;
Without this, we cannot recover;
Advise me: what kind of being is that?

## Third Response. <note>original Latin: "Responſio Tertia"</note>

One and four are five, rightly so;
But three and one are four, poorly;
If you like the three, then bring them into one;
If you cannot do that, you make nothing.

## ANOTHER RIDDLE OF FR. <note>Abbreviation for "Frater," meaning Brother or Friar.</note>
### Basil Valentine. <note>original Latin: "Basilij Valentini." Basil Valentine was a legendary 15th-century alchemist, purportedly a Benedictine monk, though his works likely date to the 1600s.</note>

Five books were prepared for us
By Moses alone, through God’s creation.
A smaller number follows his books,
Of what was commanded there to his people.
Three silent Patriarchs
Explain it all in one sum;
One witness speaks with the loudest voice,
He who is worth nothing is empty in mind.
Fifty is a greater number than five,
And yet there are only two throughout.
A thousand concludes the end at once;
Whoever understands this rightly is truly rich.
Five things in life reveal this,
And five in death were also present;
Four of them speak the judgment,
While one alone settles the <term>conflict</term>. <note>original: "Strauß." In this period, it refers to a fight, struggle, or dispute rather than a bouquet of flowers.</note>

## ANOTHER RIDDLE. <note>original Latin: "ALIVD AENIGMA."</note>

Seven letters are set:
At the front 50, then a hundred and one at the end;
In the middle thereof, a thousand stands.
My name thus possesses throughout
Three syllables and three vowels,
Eleven hundred fifty-one in total number. <note>This is a numerical cipher using Roman Numerals: L (50) + M (1000) + C (100) + I (1) = 1151. The seven-letter name is "ALCHIMI" (Alchemy), which contains the vowels A-I-I and the consonants L-C-H-M.</note>
There are also four consonants therein;
Now guess: what is my name?
If you now prepare me rightly,
I bring the lineage of all metals
Into their first essence, clear and pure,
And make out of them a new figure,
Which here upon this Earth
Can nevermore be separated.
